title: Forecasting from history: Monte Carlo instead of adding up estimates

videos.script: Thirty items are left on the new invoicing screen. Somebody asks when they will be done. {{question}} The usual answer adds up thirty estimates. It feels careful, and it is wrong, always in the same direction. {{adding}} It leaves out the waiting. It pretends the items happen one after another. And it adds up uncertainty as if it were a number. {{three}} There is a better way, and it is simpler than it sounds. {{better}} Take the team's real days. Two items on a Tuesday, none on a Saturday. Draw them at random to make one possible month. {{draw}} Do it ten thousand times, and you have a picture of every month that is plausible. {{picture}} This lesson builds that simulation on your computer, in two short programs. One answers how many by a date. One answers by when. {{programs}} Then it changes which history the simulation believes, and the date moves by two weeks. That is the part to remember. {{window}}
